title: Octopus Mirror Engine
outcome: Compare nine views of one record and explain which steps are actual proof-of-work checks.
show: Draw a three-by-three grid. Rows are forward, backward, and inverted. Columns are this side of the mirror, as the mirror, and the other side of the mirror.
concepts: Use the forward pass to record what goes in and comes out. Use the backward view to trace a receipt to its inputs. Hash verification recomputes from the original bytes.
For the classroom example, invert the acceptance predicate to list rejects. Byte-order conversion between Bitcoin’s displayed hash and serialized bytes is a separate representation issue.

The project names eight arms: intake, forward, reverse, distribute, optimize, refine, Golden Goose, and conductor. They can model separate queues or stages. Mining hardware still tests candidate headers against the network target. Reordering changes which guesses are visited first.

These names come from the original biological metaphor. In a computing system, define the actual operation and measure its result, such as filtering duplicates or comparing a candidate hash to its target. Pending transactions and orphaned blocks confer no automatic ownership or payout.
replicate: Use candidate values 7, 17 and 4 with target 10. Run them forward and backward and invert the predicate for a reject list.
Fill this side with inputs, as the mirror with verification, and the other side with receipts. Compare normalized pass and reject sets for each order.
check: What remains true if the same guesses are checked in reverse order?
The same guesses satisfy the target. Receipt order can change, while the target and accepted set stay the same.
sources: Octopus Mirror Engine · Nathan Tabor project

challenge.title: Work the nine views

challenge.tip: Here, backward changes encounter order. Inverted flips the classroom acceptance test and lists rejects.
